dataset.name: CROCUS Optical All Precipitation Gauge Data at Argonne National Laboratory Prairie Site
description: The APG (Optical Scientific Inc. All-Precipitation Gauge 815-DS) dataset contains one-minute measurements of precipitation rate, precipitation accumulation, air temperature, and present weather detection, both in 4680 format and decoded. Data were collected at the Argonne Testbed for Multiscale Observational Science (ATMOS), a 20-acre prairie site at Argonne National Laboratory in Lemont, Illinois. The data is presented as daily NetCDF (.nc) files, each containing approximately 24 hours of observations. Files follow the naming convention of: the project (CROCUS), location (atmos), instrument name (apg), data level (raw, a1), and date (year, month, day). The NetCDF format can be accessed using common scientific software such as Python using xarray, netCDF4 or act-doe.

measurementTechnique: The APG is mounted in an East/West orientation on a 3m tripod at Argonne's ATMOS site, specifically in the rain field location. The receiver end is pointing towards the east direction, as specified in the instrument manual. There are no near by blockages to the APG in any direction and can receive clear and open signal path for measurements.

Data is collected on a Campbell CR1000x data longer with a sample rate of 1 minute. Data is manually collected from the CR1000x on a monthly basis and is then processed from a .dat file to the .nc file using Python and the xarray package. Additional meta data, including units, are added into the data files at that time. The DOE-ACT python package is used to decode the 4680 meteorological codes provided by the instrument to translate it into a string value for the current weather detected, such as 'No significant weather observed' or "Drizzle, not freezing, slight".

Known limitation of the data: The precipitation accumulation variable does not reset after it hit 1000 mm and continues to oscillate around that value. This is an issue that has not been resolved, and the manufacturer is working on a firmware fix. The precipitation accumulation hit its max value on April 7th, 2024. It is recommended to use the precipitation rate to derive an accumulation after that date. The precipitation accumulation is also a running total from when the instrument was installed, therefore the precipitation accumulation variable should be normalized for each day if the accumulation total is to be used, otherwise the precipitation rate variable provides the running accumulation without normalization.

Known Limitation of the data: The temperature measurements are only given as a whole number, such as 19, 10, or 0. The present weather precipitation detection is impacted by the whole number temperature and in some instances, freezing rain at 0 degC may be identified as snow, or snow as freezing rain if temperatures are 0.5 degC.
No other data QCing is performed as there is no known correctable instrument bias during specific precipitation event types.

For variables within the datafiles:
APG_PW_Code: WMO Present Weather Condition Code,
APG_Precip_Rate: Instantaneous Precipitation Rate, units: 'mm/hr',
APG_Precip_Accum: Precipitation Accumulation, units: 'mm',
APG_Temp: APG Temperature Probe, units: 'degC',
APG_PW_Code_decoded: WMO Present Weather Condition Code, Decoded present weather values
